items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: Then on the younger side, we had men like...I think it was Kenny Kersey; and Milton Fletcher on trumpet; and Joe Guy; Eddie Vinson...

ctx.x: Yeah, there was Louis Bacon, trumpet. He was from Russell's band, too! Also Chick Webb's band he was from. And he was also the vocalist in Cootie's band. He had a wonderful bass voice. Wonderful.

Then on the younger side, we had men like...I think it was Kenny Kersey; and Milton Fletcher on trumpet; and Joe Guy; Eddie Vinson... Well, Bob Dorsey, I would put him with the younger boys, because he was a nut. He was a real nut. In fact, all of the young ones, they were nuts. Believe me. They didn't care about anything. But they could play.

Oh, Kenny Kersey wasn't there. Or was he? Yeah, I guess Kenny Kersey did open the band. I really don't know who opened... Yeah, he opened up the band. Yeah, I think Kenny Kersey did open the band, because (?)Rich Carter(?) came along later, when we went into the Savoy... Bud Powell. Bud Powell came along later. But anyway, Ken Kersey was all right. He didn't bother nobody.
